title: Rank-one weights
statement:
Every rank-one lisse Weil sheaf on a smooth geometrically connected
curve is punctually $\iota$-pure ([sk-d-real-weights]). For $c=\chi(s)$ its
weight is $\lambda_\iota(c)=2\log_q|\iota(c)|$.

*Complement.* For any degree-one lift $s$ and $z=\chi(s)$, the functions
$w\mapsto z^{\deg w}$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}(w)=\chi(w)z^{-\deg w}$ are
characters, $\chi=\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}\cdot z^{\deg}$,
$\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}(s)=1$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}(W(U_0))=\chi(P)$
([det-p-rankone], [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve]).

steps.text:
Put $\varepsilon(w)=\chi(w)c^{-\deg w}$. If $w=gs^d$ with $g\in P$,
then $\varepsilon(w)=\chi(g)$, and hence $\varepsilon$ has finite image
by [sk-p-real-rankone] ([det-p-rankone]). At a closed point $x$ the
eigenvalue is $\varepsilon(F_x)c^{d(x)}$. The first factor has finite
order, hence complex absolute value one ([lem-tw-root-of-unity-modulus]), so
the eigenvalue has absolute value $q_x^{\lambda_\iota(c)/2}$
([cor-wf-rank-one-punctual-purity-curve]). Changing $s$ multiplies $c$ by a
value of $\chi$ on $P$, which has finite order, and so it does not
change this number.
